newsitem.title: USA: Mass declares state of emergency for part of state.
newsitem.headline: Mass declares state of emergency for part of state.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld declared Monday a state of emergency for the eastern part of the state that was hit hard by floods, sending residents to shelters and shutting several local schools.
"If anyone has the fortitude to brave out this storm it is the New Englander," said Weld, in prepared remarks.

"But it is going to take a lot of elbow grease and a lot of patience to wade through some of the most severe flooding we've seen in a long time," he added, promising to keep public safety and health officials working around the clock.
The state's public safety and environmental officials are checking flooded area schools and some dams, which are overburdened and poised to collapse, Weld said.

Should Horn Pond Dam in Woburn, which is in danger of failing, be breached, more severe flooding would threaten Woburn and neighboring Winchester, as well as towns along the Mystic River, including Arlington, Medford and Somerville.
The storm, which has closed many roadways throughout the state, also has disrupted public transportation in areas.
